reason: The hypothesis directly combines two well-documented strategies from the literature—microstructural inversion (P7) and boron-induced grain-boundary strengthening (P12, P18, P29)—and applies them to the NbMoTaW system, which has not been studied with either approach. However, the combination is a straightforward additive transfer of known interventions to a new alloy, and the mechanism (coherent precipitates in a ductile BCC matrix trapping defects) is stated almost verbatim from the source passages, without resolving any conflict or proposing a new mechanistic link. The irradiation tolerance claim merely extends the known precipitate-trapping concept (P5) to this system. Therefore, the core idea is a synthesis of existing findings but lacks a non-trivial leap beyond the combined sources.
copied_elements: microstructural inversion from continuous B2 to continuous BCC with discrete precipitates (P7, P11, P25)
adding 0.1 at.% boron to improve grain boundary cohesion and ductility (P12, P18, P29)
boron-induced intergranular boride precipitation (P12, P18, P29)
trapping He bubbles at second phase precipitates (P5)
improved room-temperature ductility without compromising high-temperature strength (P7, P20)
